Violated invariant: the default path consumes the kind byte (3714 'int opcode = *ptr++') and then dereferences 'opsize = *ptr++' (3724) with NO 'if (length < 2) return;' guard between the two reads; the only checks, opsize<2 (3725) and opsize>length (3727), run AFTER the length byte was already fetched, so they cannot prevent the over-read. When length==1 (a one-byte trailing option whose kind is neither EOL nor NOP - fully attacker-constructible because doff counts in 4-byte units and NOP/EOL handling only adjusts length by exactly 1 per byte), the loop reads one byte past the end of the TCP option area. Unsafe use: the OOB byte is consumed as opsize and compared/used for loop bookkeeping (ptr += opsize-2; length -= opsize at 3810-3811), i.e. an unvalidated, out-of-bounds value drives subsequent pointer advance. Consequence: one-byte out-of-bounds read of skb memory immediately after the TCP header (KASAN-detectable slab over-read / info leak adjacent to packet data). Counterevidence checked: this is exactly the pre-9609dad263f8 shape that upstream fixed by inserting 'if (length < 2) return;' before 'opsize = *ptr++' (the same fix the seed commit 07718be26568 ported to mptcp_get_options, whose changelog cites 9609dad263f8); sibling walks in this tree (nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c tcp_options/tcp_sack at 398/459) DO have the guard, proving the guard is the expected invariant and its absence in tcp_input.c is a genuine divergence, not an upstream design choice. Impact uncertainty: the byte lies in skb-adjacent memory that is normally still within the skb linear allocation, so the leak is one byte of packet-adjacent data; reported as a structural, line-verified match with the seed mechanism.

Untrusted source: TCP option bytes of a received segment parsed by tcp_parse_md5sig_option(const struct tcphdr *th) (3866), called from tcp_v4_rcv (tcp_ipv4.c:657), tcp_v4_send_reset (1239), tcp_v6_do_rcv/send_reset (tcp_ipv6.c:700/922) whenever CONFIG_TCP_MD5SIG is enabled - every received TCP packet with MD5 keys configured. Violated invariant: identical shape to tcp_parse_options; the initial 'length < TCPOLEN_MD5SIG' shortcut (3872) bounds only the first iteration's budget, and after options are consumed length can reach 1, at which point the default path reads 'opsize = *ptr++' (3886) one byte past the option area with no remaining>=2 guard; the combined check 'opsize < 2 || opsize > length' (3887) happens after the fetch. Unsafe use: opsize is returned/compared against TCPOLEN_MD5SIG (3890) and used for 'ptr += opsize - 2; length -= opsize' (3892-3893). Consequence: one-byte OOB read past the TCP header end into packet-adjacent skb memory, same class as the seed. Counterevidence/limitations: the read byte only decides whether an MD5 option is accepted (returns ptr or NULL) and the fetched value is never echoed to the attacker, so the leak is a value-influenced control-flow decision rather than a direct info disclosure; reported as a structural match with medium confidence.

Untrusted source: TCP option bytes of any packet traversing a SYNPROXY rule (net/ipv4/netfilter/ipt_SYNPROXY.c:278/366/395, net/ipv6/netfilter/ip6t_SYNPROXY.c:292/387/416), fetched via skb_header_pointer(skb, doff + sizeof(*th), length, buf) into the fixed stack buffer 'u8 buf[40]' (line 35) with length = (th->doff * 4) - sizeof(*th) up to 40. Violated invariant: synproxy_parse_options() (nf_synproxy_core.c:31) consumes the kind byte (43 'int opcode = *ptr++') then executes 'opsize = *ptr++' (53) with no 'length < 2' check between the two reads; the opsize<2 (54) and opsize>length (56) guards run only after the fetch. When the final option byte is the only remaining byte (length==1) and its kind is not EOL/NOP, the loop reads buf[40] - one byte past the end of the 40-byte on-stack buffer (attacker constructs this by setting doff=15 so length==40 and making the 40th option byte a non-EOL/non-NOP kind). Unsafe use: the OOB byte becomes opsize, is compared against length, and drives 'ptr += opsize - 2; length -= opsize' plus MSS/WSCALE/TIMESTAMP body reads (get_unaligned_be16/be32 of ptr). Consequence: one-byte stack out-of-bounds read (KASAN stack-buffer-overflow class) of uninitialized/adjacent stack memory whose value influences option parsing. Counterevidence checked: the sibling netfilter walkers nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c tcp_options (line 398) and tcp_sack (line 459) contain exactly the 'if (length < 2) return;' guard that this function lacks, confirming the missing invariant is a real divergence within the same subsystem; skb_header_pointer returns buf only after copying 'length' bytes, so the over-read is provably at index length<=40 of a 40-byte array.

Untrusted source: TCP option bytes of packets matched by an xt_tcpmss ('tcpmss') rule, fetched via skb_header_pointer(skb, par->thoff + sizeof(*th), optlen, _opt) into the fixed stack buffer 'u8 _opt[15 * 4 - sizeof(_tcph)]' (=40 bytes, xt_tcpmss.c:40) with optlen = th->doff*4 - sizeof(*th). Consequence: one-byte out-of-bounds read - when optlen==40 it reads _opt[40] past the 40-byte stack buffer (KASAN stack OOB), and for shorter optlen it reads the first byte of _opt beyond the copied region (uninitialized stack). cake_get_tcpopt() (net/sched/sch_cake.c:953) is a TCP-option walk with exactly the seed's shape and, unlike every other walk in s02, has NO 'if (length < 2)' check between consuming the kind byte (line 961 'int opcode = *ptr++;') and dereferencing the size byte (line 970 'opsize = *ptr++;'). Untrusted source: attacker-controlled TCP header options of queued packets examined by the qdisc ACK filter (cake_ack_filter, caller at lines 1169/1192/1241/1252); cake_get_tcphdr copies min(hdr_len,64) bytes of the packet into the on-stack buffer '_tcph[64]' (declared line 1153) via skb_header_pointer. Missing guarantee: the loop condition is 'while (length > 0)', the EOL/NOP fast path only does 'length--' for NOP, so when length==1 and the last byte is any kind other than EOL/NOP the switch/ifs fall through to 'opsize = *ptr++' which reads 1 byte past the option area derived from th->doff (i.e. past __tcp_hdrlen(tcph)-20 bytes). If doff*4 < 60 the option area ends inside the 64-byte stack buffer, so the over-read stays within _tcph (the tcp_parse_aligned_timestamp-style 'safe padding' shape); but when th->doff==15 (60-byte header) length can reach 44 and __tcp_hdrlen-20 == 40, leaving 4 slack bytes in the 64-byte buffer, so a trailing 1-byte option still over-reads within the copy; the OOB becomes actual out-of-object only for the non-linear/large-header corner cases where the direct skb pointer path (skb_header_pointer returning skb->data) is used and doff*4 exceeds the copied length boundary. Counterevidence checked: opsize is then validated ('opsize < 2 || opsize > length' breaks), so no wide over-read; the mirrored walk in cake_tcph_may_drop (lines 1097-1107) has the identical missing length>=2 check. Because the direct byte-past-buffer read is only reachable when the 64-byte copy is not the limiting factor, confidence is medium rather than high; the invariant 'at least 2 bytes remain before reading the size byte' is nonetheless violated in the source.

ip6_parse_tlv() (used by ipv6_destopt_rcv and ipv6_rthdr_rcv for hop-by-hop/destination options of remotely received IPv6 packets) walks attacker-controlled TLV bytes: at loop entry with len==1 it reads the type byte nh[off] via the switch and then dereferences nh[off + 1] as the option length with no 'len >= 2' check between consuming the type byte and reading the length byte - structurally identical to the seed mptcp_get_options OOB (the 'optlen > len' clamp only happens later, in the default case, after the length byte is already read). Whether this is a real OOB depends on whether nh[off+1] lies inside the linear data area: the caller does pskb_may_pull() of the full hdrlen before ip6_parse_tlv(), so hdrlen bytes ending at skb_transport_offset+hdrlen are linear; when len==1 the final TLV ends exactly at that boundary, making nh[off+1] read one byte past the pulled header region and potentially past the skb linear length for a packet whose option header ends exactly at the end of linear data. Exploitability is unproven (the byte is usually within the skb head allocation), hence low confidence, but the missing remaining>=2 guard is exactly the invariant the seed fixed.

br_nf_check_hbh_len() (bridge netfilter IPv6 validation of forwarded hop-by-hop headers, untrusted input on any bridged port) has the same shape: when len==1 the switch reads the type byte nh[off] (IPV6_TLV_PAD1 case sets optlen=1, but IPV6_TLV_PADN falls through and every other type hits the default case) and 'int optlen = nh[off + 1] + 2' has already dereferenced nh[off+1] before any remaining>=2 check; the only guard, 'if ((raw + len) - skb->data > skb_headlen(skb)) goto bad', bounds the header extent but does not guarantee two bytes remain for the final TLV. Same seed-equivalent missing invariant; impact bounded similarly (reads within/just past the linear skb region), hence low confidence.

This is structurally identical to the seed mptcp_get_options missing 'if (length < 2) return' between the kind byte and the size byte. Counterevidence/uncertainty: no runtime KASAN reproducer was built (read-only snapshot, no kernel build environment); whether the one-byte read crosses a real object boundary depends on skb head allocation/tailroom, so actual OOB impact is unproven - hence low confidence, same classification the sibling s01 audit (fact f002) gave the identical code shape.

Untrusted source: a2mp_chan_recv_cb() iterates A2MP signalling commands received over the L2CAP A2MP fixed channel (net/bluetooth/a2mp.c:603); every byte of hdr (code/ident/len) and the command payload is attacker-controlled remote Bluetooth data. Counterevidence checked: the same file's per-command handlers (a2mp_discover_req/rsp etc.) consistently guard 'le16_to_cpu(hdr->len) < sizeof(*req)' and 'while (len >= sizeof(*cl))' with matching skb_pull of le16_to_cpu(hdr->len) at lines 466/546/598, so the body walks themselves are clamped; the over-read is confined to the 1-2 byte hdr->code/hdr->ident re-dereference on the shared error path (info is not propagated to the peer -- BT_DBG only, and hdr->ident only echoes back a byte the attacker supplied -- so impact is an OOB read visible to KASAN/UMR detectors rather than a proven info leak).

The loop CONDITION itself dereferences the element length byte tmp_old[1] with no check that at least 2 bytes remain: when the walk lands on the final lone byte (offset ielen-1, e.g. a truncated last MBSSID-derived element), tmp_old[1] reads one byte past the end of the ie buffer, exactly the seed mechanism (kind byte consumed, size byte read while remaining==1). tmp_old advances by attacker-chosen tmp_old[1]+2 sums, so landing on ielen-1 is fully attacker-controlled; the id byte at 308 is then also used for the WLAN_EID_EXTENSION/WLAN_EID_VENDOR_SPECIFIC decisions. Counterevidence checked: memcpy at scan.c:326/346 is bounded by the same <= ielen condition, so the OOB is the length-byte read itself; no caller validates trailing bytes before this walk.

Second loop of the same cfg80211_gen_new_ie: sub_copy is kmemdup(profile, profile_len) (scan.c:283), where profile is the attacker-controlled merged MBSSID profile produced by cfg80211_merge_profile from remote beacon data. The condition dereferences sub_copy[tmp_new - sub_copy + 1] as the length byte without a remaining>=2 guard; if the profile ends with a lone element-ID byte, sub_copy[subie_len] is a 1-byte out-of-bounds read past a heap kmalloc allocation (KASAN-detectable), and that attacker-influenced value then drives the memcpy at line 370 and the cursor advance at line 375. Same seed shape: element-id consumed, size byte read when fewer than 2 bytes remain; no trailing-length validation exists between merge and this walk.

skip_ie explicitly assumes 'a validly formed IEs buffer' but is reached from ieee80211_ie_split/ieee80211_ie_split_ric (util.c:1592-1637) whose callers pass nl80211-supplied buffers (net/mac80211/mlme.c:933/969/995 assoc_data->ie, net/mac80211/tdls.c:391+ extra_ies), which userspace can end with a lone element-ID byte. The outer loop only checks pos < ielen before reading the id byte ies[pos]; skip_ie then unconditionally reads ies[pos+1] (and again at 1585 for fragments) without confirming pos+1 < ielen, a 1-byte OOB read when exactly one byte remains, and advances pos by an unvalidated 2+len. Counter-evidence: source is a privileged local user (CAP_NET_ADMIN for nl80211), not fully remote, hence medium confidence; the RIC inner loop's own id reads at util.c:1607/1623 are guarded by (pos+ext) >= ielen.

Untrusted source: user-supplied IEs passed to ieee80211_ie_split_ric (cfg80211.h:9774 ieee80211_ie_split -> mlme.c:1675/1681 ieee80211_add_before_ht_elems with assoc_data->ie, and mlme.c:2369 ieee80211_ie_split_vendor with assoc_data->ie from wext/nl80211 assoc request). Untrusted source: TCP options bytes of a packet traversing a CAKE qdisc (ack-filter path). cake_get_tcpopt walks the option area after consuming the kind byte and immediately dereferences '*ptr++' to read the opsize field with NO 'if (length < 2) break;' guard between the two reads - exactly the invariant violation fixed for mptcp_get_options/tcp_parse_options (seed class, upstream fix 9609dad263f8 shape). When length==1 the loop reads the opcode, then executes opsize = *ptr++ one byte past the end of the option area. Reachability: cake_get_tcphdr (line 949-950) fetches only min(__tcp_hdrlen(tcph), bufsize) bytes with bufsize==64 (stack buffers _tcph/_tcph_check at lines 1154-1155); for a TCP header with doff > 16 the option walk is driven by the full __tcp_hdrlen-derived length but runs over a 64-byte stack buffer, so reads past byte 64 hit adjacent stack memory (uninitialized/adjacent-variable info leak, KASAN stack-out-of-bounds on doff<=16 truncated packets). The same unguarded shape is duplicated in cake_tcph_may_drop (lines 1097-1109). Counterevidence checked: the main in-tree TCP option walkers in this tree DO have the guard - net/ipv4/tcp_input.c tcp_parse_mss_option (line 3935), tcp_parse_options (line 3986), tcp_parse_md5sig_option (line 4154, loop precondition length >= TCPOLEN_MD5SIG and opsize<2||opsize>length check), net/mptcp/options.c mptcp_get_options (line 359, seed already fixed here), net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c (lines 358, 420) and net/netfilter/nf_synproxy_core.c (line 53); only sch_cake's copy of the walker lacks it. Note the guard also clamps option advance: without the length<2 return, a length==1 trailing opcode byte is consumed as opsize; body reads such as get_unaligned_be32(ptr) in cake_tcph_may_drop TCPOPT_TIMESTAMP (line 1124) remain gated by opsize==TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP, so the primary over-read is the unguarded opsize byte plus walk-past-buffer when header data was truncated to the 64-byte stack buffer.

Untrusted source: DCCP packet header option bytes fetched via skb_header_pointer(skb, protoff+optoff, optlen, dccp_optbuf) into dccp_optbuf (line 53), i.e. remotely attacker-controlled wire bytes of length optlen = dh->dccph_doff*4 - __dccp_hdr_len(dh). Violated invariant: the walk in dccp_find_option() (used by xt_dccp match) consumes a type byte op[i] and, whenever op[i] >= 2, dereferences op[i+1] as the option size byte without first confirming that 2 bytes remain, and then advances the cursor by that unclamped size. Unlike the sibling parser net/netfilter/xt_tcpmss.c line 64, which explicitly guards 'if (op[i] < 2 || i == optlen - 1) i++;' before consulting op[i+1], xt_dccp.c has no 'i == optlen - 1' check and no clamp of op[i+1] to (optlen - i). Unsafe use: when the truncated final option byte satisfies op[i] >= 2 (i.e. i == optlen-1), the expression op[i+1] reads exactly one byte past the end of the option data that was pulled; and for a size byte larger than the remaining bytes the loop index jumps past optlen, ending the loop (no OOB read in that case since the loop exits on i >= optlen). Consequence: one-byte out-of-bounds read of packet-adjacent memory in the linearized dccp_optbuf/dccp option area, KASAN-detectable, matching the seed mechanism (size-byte read with fewer than 2 bytes remaining / unclamped size use). Counterevidence checked: op is a 256*4-byte kmalloc'd static buffer (dccp_optbuf, line 165) so the over-read may land inside the allocated buffer rather than past its end when the header is non-linear or when optlen < buffer size - exact impact depends on linear vs copied path, hence medium confidence; with a fully linear skb, op points into the skb data and the read runs past the DCCP option area into payload bytes (info disclosure of one payload byte, no crash). Guard presence in all sibling TCP walkers (tcp_parse_options, tcp_parse_mss_option, mptcp_get_options, nf_conntrack tcp_options/tcp_sack, synproxy_parse_options, bpf_search_tcp_opt, xt_tcpmss, xt_TCPOPTSTRIP loop bound i < tcp_hdrlen - 1) confirms the missing 2-byte-remaining guard here is anomalous, not intentional design.
